```{python}
import inspect

import pypanelsim as pps


def show_signature(object_):
    print(f"{object_.__name__}{inspect.signature(object_)}")
```

## Outcome primitives

| Object | Untreated-outcome law |
|---|---|
| `TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome` | $\alpha_i+\gamma_t+\varepsilon_{it}$ |
| `LowRankFactorOutcome` | $\lambda_i'F_t+\varepsilon_{it}$ with configurable rank |
| `LinearFeatureOutcome` | $X_i'\beta_0+tX_i'\beta_1+\varepsilon_{it}$ |
| `UnitTrendOutcome` | $b_i t$ |
| `UnitPositionOutcome` | Unit levels around a position-dependent mean |
| `PeriodicTimeOutcome` | Repeated finite calendar pattern |
| `ARMAErrorOutcome` | Independent unit ARMA paths |
| `RandomARMAErrorOutcome` | Random stationary ARMA law shared across units |
| `ClusteredTrendOutcome` | Shared trend slope within latent unit clusters |
| `LatentSelectionOutcome` | Stable or interactive latent-factor path from ATT-DML |

```{python}
for object_ in (
    pps.TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome,
    pps.LowRankFactorOutcome,
    pps.LinearFeatureOutcome,
    pps.UnitTrendOutcome,
    pps.UnitPositionOutcome,
    pps.PeriodicTimeOutcome,
    pps.ARMAErrorOutcome,
    pps.RandomARMAErrorOutcome,
    pps.ClusteredTrendOutcome,
):
    show_signature(object_)
```

`TwoWayFixedEffectsOutcome` is an explicit public name for the additive unit
and period factor law. `LowRankFactorOutcome(rank=k)` is the general
interactive fixed-effects primitive. It records loadings, factors, the signal,
and errors in component metadata.

## Feature primitives

`CorrelatedGaussianFeatures` draws Toeplitz-correlated Gaussian covariates or
uses an explicit positive-definite covariance matrix. Its callable transform
can alter features used by assignment and outcomes. When
`estimator_uses_raw=True`, `PanelDataset.unit_covariates` retains the raw
features.

```{python}
show_signature(pps.CorrelatedGaussianFeatures)
show_signature(pps.LatentGradientFeatures)
```

`att_dml_nonlinear_basis()` appends the three nonlinear terms from the
ATT-DML experiment. `LatentGradientFeatures` implements the position-dependent
latent-factor distribution from its factor-selection study.

## Effect profiles

The package exposes constant, linear, concave, saturating, hump, and sinusoidal
profile functions. `EventTimeProfileEffect` converts any callable profile into
an effect model. `GaussianCellEffect`, `RandomUnitEffect`, and
`RandomWalkEffect` use the effect random stream.

Every effect model returns two related objects:

$$
\texttt{treatment_effect}_{it}
=\texttt{effect_surface}_{it}W_{it}.
$$

The first is the realized causal contribution to observed outcomes. The
second is the full effect law implied by the component.

## `PanelTruth`

Every dataset exposes `panel.truth`.

| Method | Columns |
|---|---|
| `cohort_event()` | cohort, event time, calendar time, cohort size, support, effect |
| `event_study()` | event time, supported target effect, cohort count, target unit count |
| `att_by_cohort()` | cohort ATT, unit count, treated-cell count |

`event_study(weighting="cohort_size")` uses the realized cohort sizes.
`weighting="equal_cohort"` gives each supported cohort equal weight. Neither
mode extrapolates unsupported cohort-event cells.

## Identifiers and annotations

`PanelSimulator` accepts explicit `unit_ids`, `time_ids`, `unit_annotations`,
and `time_annotations`. It always adds `ever_treated` and `adoption_period` as
unit annotations. Assignments with category metadata also add
`assignment_category`.

```python
columns = panel.as_long_dict(
    include_effect_surface=True,
    include_annotations=True,
)
```

The default long schema is unchanged. The effect surface and annotations are
opt-in columns.

## Named random streams

```{python}
show_signature(pps.SimulationSeeds)
```

`SimulationSeeds.from_seed(42)` spawns separate streams for unit features,
assignment, time features, untreated outcomes, and effects.

```python
streams = pps.SimulationSeeds.from_seed(42)
panel = simulator.simulate(streams=streams)
```

Adding an unrelated component does not shift assignment draws under this
contract. `simulate(seed=42)` retains the original shared-stream behavior for
exact backward compatibility with the canonical designs.
